title: Trigonometry
shortDescription: Ratios, standard angles, identities, complementary angles, heights and distances.
genZNote: SOH-CAH-TOA plus one table. Once 30°, 45°, 60° are in your head, half the paper is free marks.

sections.heading: Ratios and Standard Values
sections.body: sin = opposite/hypotenuse; cos = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan = opposite/adjacent; cosec, sec, cot are reciprocals.

sections.heading: Identities
bullets: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
Complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ; tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

sections.heading: Heights and Distances
bullets: Angle of elevation: line of sight above horizontal; depression: below horizontal.
tan θ = height / horizontal distance. Tower: 30° elevation at 30 m → height = 30 tan 30° = 10√3 ≈ 17.3 m.
Draw a right triangle; label known and unknown; use tan for height/base problems; for two observation points set two equations.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Trigonometry relates angles of right triangles to side ratios and solves height and distance problems.

commonTraps: Do not mix degrees and radians.

sources.name: Standard quantitative aptitude reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Quantitative Aptitude)
